quizzes.stem: A developer asks Claude for a data-import function, pastes it into the codebase and ships it after a glance because it reads cleanly. Which habit did the developer skip?

options.a: Responsibility: tell the users that an AI assisted with the release
options.b: Delegation: hand the whole function to a different person to write instead
options.c: Description: phrase the request as a longer, more detailed paragraph
options.d: Discernment: execute it against realistic cases and inspect the results

explanation.d: The builder's costly mistake is "Shipping unrun output", and the natural check is to "Run it, test it, review it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A builder is someone who owns the whole arc from a customer's problem to a shipped solution", so the function is theirs to verify.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the weight for builders falls on "Discernment of code and user experience", and a longer request does not test the result.
explanation.a: Ruled out because telling users is honest but does not test anything, and the natural check is to "Run it, test it, review it".

quizzes.stem: A university student drafts a graded argumentative essay. The course allows AI help for planning only, and they want to find where their case is weakest. Which use fits?

options.a: Ask Claude for a model paragraph on their topic, then rewrite it in their voice
options.b: Have Claude draft their weakest section, cite it as a source, and write the rest themselves
options.c: Paste the essay prompt and keep only the sentences that match their view
options.d: Ask Claude to challenge their outline, then do all the writing themselves

explanation.d: A student uses Claude as a partner by questioning the plan while the thinking and the writing stay theirs.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "writing the analysis with Claude and submitting it defeats the point and may breach the
   institution's rules", and rewording a model paragraph still hands the thinking over.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because the
   student does not delegate "the thinking the course exists to build", and a citation does not return it.
explanation.c:
is
   ruled out because "one who submits its essay as their own is not" using it as a partner, and selecting sentences
   keeps that authorship problem.

quizzes.stem: A teacher asks Claude for a quiz on a unit and gets ten questions. Which step best reflects discernment and ownership?

options.a: Share it with the class so the pupils can find any faults
options.b: Trust it, because the model wrote a similar quiz last month
options.c: Check the answers and their fit with the stated outcome
options.d: Ask Claude to rate how correct its own questions are

explanation.c: Discernment is judging accuracy and alignment with the stated outcome, and the educator owns what students are taught.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the educator "Checks: accuracy of the content taught", and a past good quiz does not show this one is right.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the educator "Owns: what students are taught, how they are assessed and the fairness of grades", and passing the checking to pupils gives that up.
explanation.d: Ruled out because asking Claude to mark itself is not the check, and the page lists "accuracy of the content taught" among the things the educator checks personally.

quizzes.stem: A non-profit's analyst must show a funder where demand is highest, using a sheet of beneficiaries' names, addresses and health notes. Policy restricts sharing personal data. Which approach fits?

options.a: Summarise it to district counts, then verify those counts
options.b: Paste ten full records first to test the method on a sample
options.c: Switch to a faster, cheaper model for the sensitive records
options.d: Upload the full sheet and ask Claude to leave names out of its findings

explanation.a:
The best answer anonymises or aggregates first and checks the results, and the funder's question needs
   areas, not individuals.
explanation.d:
Ruled out because the rule is "classify first, remove identifiers before
   analysis", and leaving names out of the findings does not keep them out of the upload.
explanation.b:
is ruled out because
   "Donor and beneficiary records are sensitive", so ten full records are still exposure.
explanation.c:
is ruled out because
   "High-volume, low-stakes drafting suits a faster, cheaper model", and the tier chosen does not change the class
   of the data.

quizzes.stem: A small shop owner has Claude draft replies to customers about delivery times. One reply promises delivery in two days, a figure the owner never supplied. What is the best response?

options.a: Stop using Claude for customer contact altogether, starting today
options.b: Send it, as the draft sounded confident and professional enough
options.c: Ask Claude whether the figure is right, and send if it agrees
options.d: Check each date and commitment against the actual policy

explanation.d: A reply that states a date is a promise the owner holds, so each date is checked against the actual policy.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the check is "that a confident reply to a customer is not invented", so confidence proves nothing.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A small owner has no one else to catch the error", and asking the same tool whether it is right does not check the policy.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "High-volume, low-stakes drafting suits a faster, cheaper model" with a spot check, so stopping altogether is not needed.

quizzes.stem: An illustrator wants to use Claude on a picture-book project and cares about being recognised for their style. Which use fits best?

options.a: Ask it to generate the whole story in their style, then sign it
options.b: Hand it production tasks, and keep the ideas and final choices
options.c: Have it write the narrative and present the result as unaided work
options.d: Let it decide the visual direction, since it knows many styles

explanation.b: Delegate production and keep authorship, the page's guidance for makers.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the maker keeps "the part that makes the work theirs", and a whole story signed by the maker is not that.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Disclosure matters more here than in many fields", and presenting AI work as unaided is the opposite.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "For a maker the distinctive voice is the product", and the visual direction is part of it.

quizzes.stem: Two staff members each receive a readable draft from Claude: a lesson rubric for one, a funding appeal for the other. Which pair of checks matches what each of them owns?

options.a: First: reading level and layout; second: tone and brand voice
options.b: First: pupils' reactions once it is handed out; second: donors' reactions once it is sent
options.c: First: accuracy and outcome fit; second: impact claims against sources
options.d: First: Claude's own rating of its accuracy; second: Claude's own rating of its sources

explanation.c:
The educator checks accuracy and alignment with the outcome, and the fundraiser checks impact claims
   against the source.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because the educator's checks include "alignment with the stated outcome",
   which reading level and layout do not cover, and they leave out "accuracy of the content taught".
explanation.b:
Ruled out because the educator "Owns: what students are taught, how
   they are assessed and the fairness of grades", and the fundraiser must check "every claim about impact, every
   statistic and every funder requirement against the source" before the audience reacts.
explanation.d:
is ruled out because
   the page lists "Impact claims and statistics against source" as the check that matters most, and a self-rating is
   not a comparison with a source.

quizzes.stem: A freelancer working for a charity wants Claude to write personalised thank-you notes that cite each supporter's past gifts, working from the full supporter list. Charity policy says personal data may not leave its systems unprotected. What should happen first?

options.a: Send twenty complete records to test the tone of the notes
options.b: Strip names and addresses, then use templates with merge fields
options.c: Pick a faster, cheaper model, since thanks are low-stakes drafting
options.d: Ask Claude to confirm that it will not keep the supporters' details

explanation.b:
Donor records are sensitive, so identifiers come out before the data goes anywhere, and the notes can be
   merged afterwards.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "the best answer anonymises or aggregates first and checks results",
   and twenty complete records are still personal data.
explanation.d:
Ruled out because "Donor and beneficiary records are
   sensitive" and the rule is to "classify first, remove identifiers before analysis", which a promise from the tool
   does not replace.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "High-volume, low-stakes drafting suits a faster, cheaper model" is
   about cost, and the data class is unchanged by the tier.

quizzes.stem: A student's course bans AI help on a graded essay. A freelance illustrator's commission contract is silent on AI. Both are tempted to use Claude. What fits each of them?

options.a: The first leaves it out; the second uses it for production and says what was done
options.b: The first uses it for planning only; the second uses it and says so
options.c: The first leaves it out; the second uses it and says nothing unless a client asks
options.d: The first leaves it out; the second uses it freely and stays silent, as the contract says nothing

explanation.a:
Where a setting has a rule, follow it; where it has none, say what you did, and a maker delegates
   production while keeping authorship.
explanation.d:
Ruled out because the page says that when a setting has no rule, "say
   what you did".
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "When the setting has a rule about AI help, follow it", and a ban leaves
   no room for planning help.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Disclosure matters more here than in many fields", and the
   maker answers for audiences' and commissioners' expectations.

quizzes.stem: Claude turns a wholesaler's data sheet into allergen notes for a bakery's new product line. One note says "may contain nuts" for an item that the sheet marks nut-free. What should the owner do?

options.a: Treat it as a one-off slip and correct only that item
options.b: Ask Claude to explain how it reached that note, then trust the rest
options.c: Check every statement against its source before anything goes out
options.d: Add a line saying an AI drafted it, and publish the rest unchanged

explanation.c: A statement customers rely on is checked against the source, and one error shows the rest are unproven.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because a small owner builds in "a short list of facts to verify before sending", which means
   checking the whole notice, not one item.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because the check is "that an answer matches the actual
   policy and not a plausible one", and an explanation from the same tool is not that comparison.
explanation.d:
is ruled out
   because "the draft is the start of the judging", and a disclosure line does not correct any statement.
